strengths: Novel gravity-aligned absolute camera coordinate system that cleanly disambiguates rotational parameters without requiring a reference frame, addressing a genuine limitation of relative representations like Plücker rays

Creative data pipeline leveraging 360° panoramic videos to sample camera trajectories across the full sphere of viewpoints, effectively mitigating dataset bias toward forward-facing level-horizon views and enabling rare cinematic shots

Thoughtful null-pitch conditioning strategy that resolves text-camera entanglement through forward-facing caption generation; empirically validated with 20% and 17% relative improvements in pitch and gravity accuracy

Valuable SpatialVID-extreme benchmark addressing genuine gap in evaluation—most existing benchmarks lack diversity in extreme pitch and roll angles; carefully constructed with manual curation and roll augmentation

Strong experimental results on camera rotation metrics (pitch error nearly halved: 23.79° vs 30.88°; relative rotation error: 14.25° vs 24.56°), with convincing qualitative evidence in Figures 2 and 7
Well-executed technical approach combining SfM pose extraction, gravity annotation from panoramic metadata, and controlled ControlNet training; clear mathematical formulation and sound implementation
Clear presentation with effective figures, particularly Figure 3 (data pipeline) and Figure 4 (trajectory diversity) that communicate core ideas effectively
weaknesses: Significant data scale disparity undermines fair comparison: method trained on ~2K WEB360 videos vs. AC3D's 65K RealEstate10K videos; while acknowledged, this confound is substantial and FVD scores (896.84 vs 798.87 for PreciseCam+WAN) suggest potential quality degradation; retraining baselines on same data would strengthen claims

No translational motion support—method handles only rotation, significantly limiting expressiveness for cinematic applications requiring dolly moves and tracking shots; relegating to future work limits practical value of 'absolute camera control' claim

Yaw ambiguity remains: users cannot control world-frame yaw in absolute sense; initializing sequences at null yaw is a workaround rather than principled solution; paper underemphasizes this as fundamental limitation

Limited baseline comparisons: VD3D [3] and CameraCtrl-II [12] are cited but not compared experimentally; only AC3D and PreciseCam+WAN included; AC3D + abs. Plücker baseline performs worse than AC3D + cam. text., unexplained

Null-pitch conditioning design choices lack thorough justification: 50% ratio claimed to provide 'good balance' without ablation across different ratios; applying conflicting supervision signals (same video captioned two ways) not adequately explained or analyzed

Evaluation uses synthetic random camera trajectories during testing rather than natural trajectories from SpatialVID; while justified for testing adherence, results on natural trajectories would be more convincing; roll error not directly evaluated near poles

Quality trade-off analysis insufficient: FVD scores worse than baselines, CLIP scores lower, visual artifacts acknowledged but not deeply analyzed; unclear when this method's accuracy gains justify quality losses

Technical details deferred: φ(·) function definition only in supplementary material; no analysis of SfM error propagation or gravity estimation accuracy from panoramic video metadata; potential cascading errors not characterized
Limited generalization evidence: WAN backbone results mentioned only in supplementary material; multiple architecture comparisons would strengthen generalizability claims
Modest benchmark scale (140 test videos) smaller than RealEstate10K; no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals provided

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing genuine limitations in extreme camera control for video generation
Creative data augmentation strategy leveraging 360° panoramic videos for exhaustive sphere sampling, avoiding natural video bias toward forward-facing views
Insightful null-pitch conditioning strategy with strong empirical validation (67% pitch error increase without it), solving the prompt-camera entanglement problem
Strong camera orientation control results outperforming all dynamic video baselines (9.35° pitch error vs 15.78° next best; 11.67° gravity error vs 17.72°)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with multiple well-motivated metrics and meaningful baseline comparisons
Two novel benchmarks for extreme camera angles and prompt-camera entanglement, promised for community release
Clear presentation with effective visualizations demonstrating superiority on extreme angles
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (SfM, gravity estimation, Plucker conditioning) without significant algorithmic advance; null-pitch conditioning is creative but data-level incremental
Gravity estimation validation lacking: uses method [19] on 8 perspective crops then averages, but no independent validation or ablation on gravity estimation quality or error propagation
Heavy training data filtering (38% discarded for 'extreme acceleration' or pose estimation failure) with imprecise criteria definition, potentially introducing bias

Benchmark construction concerns: SpatialVID-extreme uses artificial roll augmentation via video warping creating test distribution misaligned with natural video; entanglement benchmark uses only 20 panoramas; manual filtering introduces unquantified subjectivity
Significant unresolved limitation: camera translation augmentation restricted to original videos; only rotations sampled on-the-fly, limiting practical generalization to novel camera paths
CLIP score trade-off not thoroughly analyzed: 20.63 vs 22.50 for UCPE, indicating semantic degradation; no user study validating whether camera control improvement justifies this trade-off

Limited ablation studies: only null-pitch conditioning ablated; missing studies on gravity estimation effects, camera encoder architecture, filtering strategies, FoV sampling design, and hyperparameter sensitivity
Generalization not adequately addressed: trained only on PanoVid YouTube subset; no zero-shot evaluation on out-of-distribution camera sequences or domain transfer analysis
Visual artifacts acknowledged (e.g., faceless man in Fig. 5) but not systematically analyzed or quantified, dismissed as future improvement
Missing computational analysis: no inference time, memory requirements, or computational cost comparisons with baselines despite training on expensive infrastructure

strengths: Well-motivated problem with elegant solution: gravity-aligned coordinate system effectively addresses extreme camera rotation limitations in existing video generation methods
Principled data generation pipeline: Leveraging 360° panoramic videos with camera pose estimation to achieve exhaustive viewpoint coverage across the full sphere is creative and well-executed

Insightful null-pitch conditioning strategy: Addresses prompt-camera entanglement by captioning upright crops; ablation shows 67% and 52% improvement in pitch and gravity error, demonstrating significant practical value

Comprehensive evaluation framework: Two novel benchmarks (SpatialVID-extreme and entanglement benchmark) with multiple metrics; superior results on all camera orientation metrics (PitchErr, GravityErr, RotErr); strong qualitative results demonstrating clear superiority on extreme angles
Excellent presentation and reproducibility: Well-written with effective visualizations; promises benchmark release; provides implementation details; transparent about limitations and future work
Practical impact: Enables previously difficult extreme camera control capabilities, useful for creators and video generation applications
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: Primarily combines existing techniques (SfM, gravity estimation, camera encoding) rather than introducing fundamentally new algorithms; should be positioned as Applied/Systems rather than Algorithms/General

Incomplete camera control: Acknowledged limitation restricts camera sampling to rotations only; users cannot freely specify translations, significantly limiting expressivity claimed as 'absolute user control'

Dataset-specific approach with limited diversity: Reduces 7,797 to 4,798 training videos (38% discarded); requires panoramic 360° videos; sampling strategy biases toward poles without principled justification; unclear generalization to other video domains

Trade-offs in evaluation metrics not adequately discussed: CLIP score drops vs baselines (20.63 vs 22.50); FVD not improved (981.0 vs 957.9 for UCPE); paper doesn't explain quality trade-off or user preference implications
Single model evaluation: Only tested on WAN-2.2 5B; no analysis of generalization to other video generation backbones; unclear transferability of approach
Null-pitch conditioning as pragmatic workaround: Forward-looking crops + 50% look-down negative prompts feel ad-hoc rather than principled; doesn't fundamentally resolve semantic-visual entanglement

Small-scale custom benchmarks: SpatialVID-extreme manually reduces 371K videos to 140; entanglement benchmark uses only 20 panoramas; artificial roll synthesis via warping doesn't reflect natural distributions; limited scale for future community use
Missing practical validations: No user studies; no computational cost analysis; limited failure case discussion; temporal consistency not explicitly evaluated; no societal impact discussion

strengths: Well-motivated use of gravity as absolute coordinate reference to disambiguate camera rotations, addressing a real limitation of relative camera encodings

Clever data pipeline leveraging 360° panoramic videos with systematic random trajectory sampling to generate training data covering extreme pitch, roll, and full rotations (out-of-distribution for standard video data)
Novel null-pitch conditioning strategy thoughtfully addresses text-camera entanglement through forward-facing caption grounding, with clear ablation evidence (35-72% improvement in pitch error)

Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple architectures (CogVideoX, WAN 2.1, WAN 2.2), camera encodings (Plücker, UCPE), and well-designed metrics (pitch error, gravity error, rotation error, translation error, CLIP, FID, FVD)
Two new evaluation benchmarks (SpatialVID-extreme for extreme angles and entanglement benchmark for prompt-camera independence) address important gaps and will benefit the community
Architecture-agnostic method generalizes across different video generation backbones and conditioning mechanisms

Strong camera orientation results: 8.36° pitch error and 10.54° gravity error (WAN 2.2 5B) substantially outperforms baselines; qualitative results (Fig. 2) clearly demonstrate advantage on extreme rotations
weaknesses: Significant unexplained data loss: 38% of training videos discarded due to pose estimation failure; filtering criteria are vague with no analysis of whether content types are disproportionately affected, undermining reproducibility

New evaluation benchmarks are small and potentially biased: SpatialVID-extreme uses only 138 manually-filtered videos; entanglement benchmark has only 20 scenes; roll annotations are artificially added via video warping rather than naturally captured

Visual quality trade-offs not adequately justified: CLIP scores decrease despite claims of better control (22.5→21.2 for WAN 2.1+UCPE); FID/FVD scores often worse than baselines (114.7 vs 109.2 for WAN 2.1); acknowledged visual artifacts (Tokyo Skytree distortions) suggest quality degradation from strong conditioning

Null-pitch conditioning appears ad-hoc: three-way crop generation with 50% look-down injection rate is not justified and lacks theoretical grounding; complexity may hinder adoption and reproducibility

Limited failure mode analysis: no discussion of why 38% of videos fail pose estimation; no qualitative failure examples; gravity estimation robustness on challenging scenes (indoor, dynamic, occlusions) not evaluated

Concurrent work (UCPE) reduces novelty: both methods use gravity-aligned coordinates; paper's contribution is mainly improved data pipeline and null-pitch conditioning, which are valuable but incremental

Translation control remains severely limited: acknowledged limitation that on-the-fly augmentation is restricted to rotations only, requiring source video translations; significantly limits applicability for dynamic scene motion

Missing critical evaluations: no user studies validating whether improved camera metrics translate to user-perceived benefit; no computational cost analysis (training time, memory, inference); limited comparison with very recent camera control methods
